newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Apr net foreign bond buying hits record high.
newsitem.headline: Japan Apr net foreign bond buying hits record high.

text.p: Net purchases of foreign bonds by Japanese investors reached 2.5783 trillion yen in April, a record high for any month, as institutional investors increased their bond investments at the start of the new business year, a Finance Ministry official said on Wednesday.
The previous record high was 2.5438 trillion yen in April 1986.
Buying of foreign bonds by retail investors was also active and contributed to the sharp rise in foreign bond investment in April, the official said.

"The factors for the increase in foreign bond investment can be summed up as the influence of (moves in) interest rates, the foreign exchange market, and (investment at) the start of a new business year," the official said.

MOF said in a statement that the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. consumer price index data on April 15 triggered buying of U.S. Treasuries, particularly those in the medium- to long-term sectors.
Net buying of foreign bonds by Japanese investors totalled 393.0 billion yen in March.
The official said the trend of heavy foreign bond buying by Japanese investors was likely to have continued in May, although exact figures for the month of May and beyond were not yet available.
